value.author: samMularczyk
value.layerInfo: Procedural paper: fibres, folds, crumple and blotches.

paperContrast: How deep the surface reads. This steepens the normal's own Z rather than remapping the output, so the shading stays physical at both ends instead of just gaining contrast.
roughness: Fine tooth. Indexed off screen pixels, not the pattern, so it stays a constant size however the layer is scaled - film grain rather than surface texture.
fibre: Curling strands in the stock. This is the ridge structure of a noise gradient, so it costs sixteen noise evaluations - by far the most expensive layer here. Leave it low unless the strands are the point.
crumples: Faceted foil-like buckling. Two cell fields multiplied, one sharp and one soft.
folds: Creases radiating from a few seed points. The field returns the vector to the nearest seed rather than a distance, so each crease perturbs the surface outward from its own origin - which is what makes them read as folds rather than as contour lines.
drops: Sparse flecks and inclusions in the stock.
seed: Changes the arrangement without changing the character.
shadowColor: Colour the surface falls to where it turns away from the light.
